newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russian empress's necklace unsold at auction.
newsitem.headline: Russian empress's necklace unsold at auction.

text.p: An emerald and diamond necklace believed to have been the gift of Russian Empress Catherine the Great to a handsome Scot went unsold at auction on Wednesday when it failed to attract high bids
But a pink cushion-shaped diamond thought to have belonged to Queen Marie Antoinette executed during the French Revolution fetched an unexpected 1,7 million Swiss francs ($1,4 million).
The two items were among the top attractions at a sale of precious jewellery by Sotheby's at the annual autumn auctions in Geneva -- a major world centre for the auction business.
The necklace, known as the "Lothian Emeralds", was offered for sale by Britain's Marquis of Lothian, and had been expected to fetch at least one million Swiss francs ($800,000).
But with the traditional Middle Eastern buyers missing, bidding stopped at 950,000 Swiss francs after opening at 700,000 francs, and the magnificent item was withdrawn.

The necklace, according to family tradition, was presented by Catherine to John Hobart, 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire, at the end of a visit to Russia in the 18th century to negotiate an Anglo-Russian treaty with the newly-crowned Empress.
Hobart, a handsome and experienced courtier, is said in memoirs of the time to have become a favourite of the Empress who showered favours on him.

The Marie Antoinette diamond, whose seller and buyer were both unidentified, is believed to have been among a packet of personal jewels given to her hairdresser for safekeeping just before she and her husband King Louis XVI were thrown into jail by the revolutionaries.

Overall, Wednesday's sale fetched a total of 38,7 million Swiss francs ($31 million), including a record 399,500 francs ($317,000) for a collection of jewellery by classic "art nouveau" designer Rene Lalique.
The collection was put on sale by its current owner, Japan's Minami art museum.

Diana Brooks, the President and Chief Executive Officer of Sotheby's said after the auction that Middle Eastern buyers, an important element in the company's sales in the past few years, were absent from the market.
"Clearly the jewellery market in the last year has changed somewhat. The good news is Asians are participating. We had significant buying from Hong Kong," she told reporters.
"We're dealing with a different market than we were six months ago. We'll have to adjust to that."
Sotheby's dealers appeared clearly disappointed that the Catherine necklace, given extensive advance billing by the auction house, did not attract strong enough interest.
The highest price of the evening was 2,5 million Swiss francs ($1,98 million) paid by a private Hong Kong buyer for a rare intense pink diamond ring of crossover design.
"It makes you lose your perspective in life, what you can do with a million dollars, when you see these people throwing it away with a wave of a hand," said an American visitor to the sale.
